license: Quotations for criticism and teaching, each with its source. In the public domain: Wicksell (1907) and the British Association's report (1907); Wicksell's German original (1898); Fisher (1911; the copies of 1912 and 1926 are scans of works published before 1930 whose libraries state no known copyright restrictions in the United States); Fisher (1930): Econlib states 'The text of this edition is in the public domain' (row f30_pd); the Dictionary of National Biography (1892). Kahn's translation (1936) and Ohlin's introduction are in copyright: only short phrases are quoted. Keynes (1883-1946), A Treatise on Money (1930): in the public domain in the United Kingdom (life plus 70 years) and, as a work published in 1930, in the United States from 2026; short passages only, as with Chapter 23's Keynes. Lange (1942): 'COPYRIGHT 1942 BY THE UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO'; short passages only. Barsky and Summers (1985): the NBER working paper carries no copyright notice of its own; short sentences only, with full credit to the authors and the NBER. Humphrey (1986), Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond, and Berg and Jonung (1998), SSE/EFI working paper: no copyright notice found; short sentences only, with credit. The Riksbank's web page and the chapters of its Historical Monetary and Financial Statistics for Sweden: Sveriges riksbank's terms for its open data: 'The Riksbank's open data is freely available and may be further used without any special consent or agreement being required. Enter source, Sveriges riksbank and date. If you have processed statistics taken from the Riksbank's website, you may not state Sveriges Riksbank as the source.' Source: Sveriges riksbank, 2026-10-16. Wikisource pages: CC BY-SA (the life dates are facts). The chapter's Chinese renders the English; the translations are the book's.

notes: Versions and readings. Wicksell's paper: the British Association's report prints a four-point abstract (rows ba_relative, ba_followed, ba_goldlead, ba_constant), the Economic Journal the full text with a postscript on the discussion at York (rows ej_palgrave to ej_par); the chapter quotes the full text. The date: the report's contents put the paper first among the papers of Friday 3 August 1906 (rows ba_friday, ba_title), Edgeworth's paper on Thursday 2 August (row ba_edgeworth). The German original of 1898 was not consulted; Interest and Prices is Kahn's translation of 1936. Fisher (1911): quoted from the 1912 reprint of the first edition; four rows (f26_*) come from the revised edition (printing of 1926), where the 1912 copy's OCR fails in the same sentences. Keynes's 'within the whole field' (row ke_fact) is quoted by Barsky and Summers as 'in the whole field' (row bs_misquote). Coates's coefficient: both copies of the Treatise print the decimal point as '-' in the OCR ('0-893'; rows ke_893, ke2_893), read as 0.893 with a probable error of 0.014. Gibson's articles: Keynes cites the Bankers' Magazine of January 1923 and November 1926 (row ke_bm), Fisher the January 1923 article, p. 15 (row f30_gibson); Gibson's own life dates are not given by either. Barsky and Summers's Table 2 (rows bs_t2_*): the text layer of the PDF has the figures in reading order, partly without points ('65' for .65); the values come from the page image (p. 8a), as the notes of the rows say; R2 is the adjusted R2 of the table. Barsky and Summers use Homer's (1977) consol yield (row bs_homer) and a British price series that links Schumpeter, Gayer-Rostow-Schwartz and, from 1846, the Sauerbeck-Statist index (row bs_prices); the chapter's recomputation uses the Bank of England's series (snapshot boe_millennium_gibson_1821_1913), so its coefficients differ somewhat. Humphrey's equations are quoted as printed (rows hu_eq5, hu_eq7); the chapter writes them in discrete time. Edvinsson and Soederberg's printed Table A8.1 (rows es_1887, es_1913) has the values of the workbook's Table I.A8.1 (snapshot riksbank_sweden_1870_1913). Joplin's year of birth is uncertain in the DNB ('1790?', row dnb_joplin).
